description: Frozen benchmark corpus v1 for Phase 2 performance evidence. Viewport geometry follows the application model: center plus authoritative spanY; spanX = spanY * width / height for the chosen raster. Magnification is 2.5 / spanY (the default viewport span). All coordinates are exact decimal strings and must never be round-tripped through binary64 inside this manifest; the harness parses them once at run time.

cases.rationale: The application's default startup viewport. Protects first use and common navigation; a balanced mix of cheap exterior, catalog periods 1-4, higher periods, and boundary filaments.
Far-field rect entirely outside the set (every sampled pixel escapes within a few iterations). Keeps exterior-heavy regression visible and cheap.
Rect fully inside the main cardioid (verified analytically and with the classifier: 100% analytic period-1 samples). Protects the analytic fast path.
Rect fully inside the period-2 disk {|c+1| < 1/4} (verified: 100% analytic period-2 samples). Protects the second analytic fast path.

Catalog mi-p3-rabbit center widened until the view contains the rabbit interior plus its boundary filaments and surrounding exterior (measured: ~64% escaped, ~29% attracting with periods 1-27, ~6% unresolved). Exercises long-lived interior orbits and the current complaint surface.

Supplied hard view near catalog mi-p4-03 at ~126x (spanY = 2.5/126 truncated to 20 significant digits). Measured mix: ~84% escaped, ~11% attracting dominated by period 4 with a period-doubling tower p8-p28, ~5% unresolved. Screenshot-derived seeds recorded as exact center+span records per plan section 9.

Supplied hard view near catalog mi-p4-01 at ~609x (spanY = 2.5/609 truncated to 20 significant digits). Measured mix: ~95% escaped with slow near-boundary pixels, ~4% attracting p4-p20, ~2% unresolved.

Supplied hard view near catalog mi-p4-06 at ~13x (spanY = 2.5/13 truncated to 20 significant digits). Measured mix: ~72% escaped, ~24% attracting (p1, p4, p8, p12 and higher), ~4% unresolved, with near-parabolic pixels whose accepted multiplier magnitude reaches 1.0 at sample precision.

Seahorse Valley at 250,000x, far beyond any cataloged component: no detected attracting cycles; ~91% escaped with slow near-boundary pixels and ~9% unresolved at the Balanced budget. Ensures heuristics fail safely and cheaply in uncataloged high-period territory.

Interior of the period-6 satellite capping the Douady rabbit's far internal ray (along the catalog rabbit center away from its cardioid root): ~97% attracting period-6 with accepted multiplier magnitudes up to ~0.81, plus a near-boundary unresolved band. Orbits with |lambda| approaching 1 correctly remain unresolved, which is the fallback behavior under test.

Elephant Valley filament comb: ~96% escaped with a slow tail (up to the 512-iteration budget), ~3% attracting on filaments at periods 15-32, ~1% unresolved. Status flips between neighboring pixels, so lanes diverge and heuristics must stay cheap.

Neighborhood of the Feigenbaum period-doubling accumulation point on the real axis: ~30% of pixels exhaust the Balanced budget (unresolved), ~67% escape slowly, and the only detected cycles sit at the period-32 cap. Ensures exhaustion stays unresolved rather than guessed.

The declared product zoom envelope: spanY is the decimal rounding of 1/2,400,000, i.e. exactly 6,000,000x against the 2.5 default span. Centered on the basilica disk's 1/2-parabolic point (-5/4, 0), an exact rational coordinate; the disk boundary is locally vertical there, splitting the shipping raster deterministically into ~50% analytic period-2 interior and ~50% near-parabolic exterior that exhausts the budget.
